questions.stem: On its balance sheet, Cedar Works lists accounts payable of $10,600, accrued liabilities of $3,900, and unearned revenue of $400. What are total current liabilities?

options.misconception: omits unearned revenue from the current liability total
reports only the smallest liability balance
subtracts one liability from another

questions.explanation: Every obligation due within a year belongs in current liabilities, so $10,600 plus $3,900 plus $400 totals $14,900. Omitting unearned revenue would understate obligations because that balance represents a duty to deliver goods or services.
questions.hint: Add every obligation that must be settled within one year.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Harborview Supply issues a $10,250 bond paying 6 percent annual interest. What is the annual cash interest payment?

options.misconception: treats the face value itself as the interest payment
uses sixty percent instead of six percent of face value
divides by the rate instead of multiplying by it

questions.explanation: Cash interest on a bond equals face value times the stated rate, so $10,250 times six percent is $615 each year. Dividing by the rate or using the face value ignores how a coupon payment is calculated.
questions.hint: Multiply face value by the stated coupon rate.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: On the treasury's bond worksheet, a $9,900 bond issued at a discount pays $693 of cash interest this period and has $140 of discount amortization. What is interest expense?

options.misconception: uses the coupon on face value rather than effective expense
uses only cash interest and ignores the discount amortization
subtracts discount amortization from cash interest

questions.explanation: When bonds are issued at a discount, interest expense exceeds the cash paid because the discount amortization is an additional financing cost, so $693 plus $140 gives $833. Subtracting the amortization would describe a premium bond instead.
questions.hint: A discount increases interest expense above the cash paid.

questions.stem: Pinecrest Partners has 72 shares of 6 percent preferred stock with a $7 par value. What is the annual preferred dividend?

options.misconception: computes the dividend on one share rather than all shares
uses sixty percent instead of six percent
uses total par value and ignores the dividend rate

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Willow Services has total stockholders' equity of $9,200, including $800 of preferred stock, and 33 shares of common stock outstanding. What is book value per common share?

options.misconception: adds preferred stock instead of deducting it
reports total common equity rather than a per-share amount
includes preferred stock in the common shareholders' claim

questions.explanation: Book value per common share divides the equity attributable to common shareholders by shares outstanding, so $9,200 less $800 divided by 33 gives $255. Preferred stock must be deducted because it belongs to a different class of owners.
questions.hint: Remove preferred equity before dividing by common shares.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: On June 17, 2026, the board of Summit Co. declares a $8,850 cash dividend to be paid later. Which entry records the declaration?

options.misconception: debits the wrong account while leaving the credit unchanged
credits the wrong account while leaving the debit unchanged
reverses the debit and credit sides of the entry

questions.explanation: Declaration creates an obligation, so Dividends is debited for $8,850 and Dividends Payable is credited. Cash is not credited at declaration because no payment has occurred yet; the cash entry is made on the payment date.
questions.hint: Declaration creates a liability; payment later removes it.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: On July 12, 2024, Summit Manufacturing repurchases its own shares from investors for $8,500 in cash. What entry records the treasury stock purchase?

options.misconception: debits the wrong account while leaving the credit unchanged

options.text: Debit Treasury Stock $8,500; credit Dividends Payable $8,500.
options.misconception: credits the wrong account while leaving the debit unchanged
reverses the debit and credit sides of the entry

questions.explanation: A repurchase of the company's own shares is recorded by debiting Treasury Stock, a contra-equity account, for $8,500 and crediting Cash. Common Stock is not reduced because the shares are not retired, and no liability arises in a repurchase.
questions.hint: Treasury stock is a contra-equity account, not a reduction of common stock.
